task.title: Tell the skill how to resolve dependency IDs into titles and verify the skill guidance changes agent behavior
task.description:
The workbook skill now tells agents to "Describe dependencies and blockers by the titles of the tasks involved." (skills/workbook/SKILL.md:35), but nothing in the skill tells the agent where those titles come from. The read procedure (skills/workbook/SKILL.md lines 12-22) ends at `workbook show <full-id> --json`, and that envelope carries dependencies as bare IDs: internal/core/task.go:146 declares `Dependencies []string` with the JSON tag `dependencies`, so a blocked task renders as "dependencies":["WB-01KYD72S4N6RB51NP2KKHGE7AD"] with no titles attached.

Failure scenario: an agent takes a task, finds it blocked, and must report why. It has been told to name the blocker by title but never told to resolve the dependency ID, so it either fabricates a plausible-sounding title or falls back to the raw ID the new section tells it not to lead with.

Fix: add a clause to the read procedure or to the dependency bullet instructing the agent to resolve each entry of data.dependencies with `workbook show <dependency-id> --json` and use that result's data.title. Also worth evaluating whether the show envelope should carry dependency titles itself, which would remove the extra round trip.

Deferred from PR #24 (branch docs/skill-task-titles, task WB-01KZC3751Q0X3RJQGRCC7NXH83) as a minor review finding. The new guidance is still a net improvement as written, and the gap is a missing follow-through rather than a regression, so it was left for a separate change.

Acceptance criterion 5 of WB-01KZC3751Q0X3RJQGRCC7NXH83 was behavioral: "An agent following the updated skill, asked to take the next task, announces it by title." PR #24 verified it only at the text level. TestSkillDocumentSeparatesMachineIDsFromHumanTitles (internal/agentdocs/render_test.go:109) asserts that specific substrings appear in the embedded skill body; it would pass identically if the guidance were phrased in a way no agent actually follows.

The repo already has a method for this kind of evidence: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-30-workbook-agent-skill.md Step 7 dispatches fresh agents with no conversation history against temporary repositories to produce GREEN evidence for skill behavior, after Step 1 captures the RED baseline. No such run was performed for the titles-over-IDs section.

Do: run the Step 1 / Step 7 RED-then-GREEN protocol for the "IDs are for commands, titles are for humans" section (skills/workbook/SKILL.md lines 24-38). Scenarios should at minimum cover announcing a selected task, reporting a lifecycle transition, and reporting an error. Record the transcripts as evidence, and if agents keep leading with the ULID, revise the section (heading placement, or fold the rule into the selection steps) until they do not.

Failure scenario if skipped: the section merges and agents keep announcing "Taking WB-01KZC..." because the guidance sits under a heading they skim past - the exact regression the original ticket was filed for - and neither CI nor the substring test would catch it.

Deferred from PR #24 (branch docs/skill-task-titles) as a minor review finding: the behavioral run is a separate multi-agent exercise rather than a code change to that PR.
